reply.text:
I can help, but "clean up" could mean several different things, and I don't want to change files you didn't mean me to touch. I'll start by looking at the repo without changing anything.

TOOL: git status --short && echo "---" && git log --oneline -n 10 && echo "---" && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | head -200

Once I see the layout and recent history, I'll suggest specific cleanup candidates, such as stray or generated files, dead code, unused dependencies, inconsistent formatting, or stale docs. Then you can tell me which ones to act on. Anything I notice outside that scope I'll list for you rather than fix.
